title: 13 sfx files were never run through sfx_soften.py (cash_pickup x3, cash_register x3, pin_crash x3, shot_heavy x3, bowl_roll): peak-normalised to -1 dBFS, unfiltered, cash_pickup_2 even clips at +0.3 dBFS
repro: Measured every audio/sfx/*.ogg (ffmpeg decode, loudest-100ms RMS, peak, >4 kHz energy share) and compared md5 against SOFTEN_LOG.json: these 13 have no log entry. Peaks -0.7..+0.3 dBFS (all softened files sit <= -1.5). bowl_roll is now the loudest non-jingle effect in the game (-12.5 dBFS RMS, -16.5 after the -4 bus vs typical -18..-22); cash_pickup_2 peak +0.3 dBFS (decoded float clips on playback); pin_crash_3 is 97% energy above 4 kHz (centroid 10.4 kHz), cash_register 91%, cash_pickup 73% (centroid 9 kHz). They were added later by cc0_import (cash_*) and make_rec_audio (pin_crash, bowl_roll) / shot_heavy import after the soften pass.
fix: Run `python3 tools/sfx_soften.py --only cash_pickup,cash_pickup_2,cash_pickup_3,cash_register,cash_register_2,cash_register_3,pin_crash,pin_crash_2,pin_crash_3,shot_heavy,shot_heavy_2,shot_heavy_3,bowl_roll` (it rm's before write, hardlink safe). Add TARGETS entries for 'cash_pickup' (-18, like coin) and 'cash_register' (-18). Then add a guard to tools/sfx_audit.py (already in check.sh): every non-j_ .ogg in audio/sfx must have a SOFTEN_LOG entry whose md5 matches, so new imports can't skip the pass again.

title: Gangster arc coin pickup (Money.SFX coin->cash_pickup) bypasses GROUP_DB coin -3 dB and was never softened: the most-heard money sound in that arc plays ~9-12 dB louder than the penguin coin and is the brightest effect in the game
repro: Music.sfx renames coin to cash_pickup before _group_db(name), so the 'coin' -3.0 group never applies (no 'cash_' key in GROUP_DB); the in-key exemption list also checks the renamed name. Measured in-game (file + -4 bus + group): coin takes -31.1/-27.9/-27.9 loudest-100ms (10 ms: -24.8/-20.0/-22.1), cash_pickup -19.3 (100 ms RMS) / -15.5 (10 ms), 0.73 of energy above 4 kHz, centroid 9.1 kHz (coin ~2.8 kHz). Every pickup in the gangster arc fires it. So a penguin-arc coin is 9-12 dB quieter than a gangster-arc bill pickup.
fix: In scripts/music.gd add "cash_": -3.0 to GROUP_DB (covers cash_pickup/cash_register/cash) or compute _group_db from the pre-swap name; add "cash_pickup" next to "coin" in the fixed-pitch list if bills should stay stable. Combine with c6_05_01 (soften the files) so the swap lands at the same loudness and brightness as the penguin coin.

title: Long footstep takes (gravel/leaves/mud/snow ~0.49 s) make Music.step drop every other step: the single step voice refuses a new step while _steps.playing, but the player fires steps every 0.25 s (run) / 0.33 s (walk)
repro: player.gd:840-847 calls Music.step every 0.25/0.33 s; music.gd step() returns early if _steps.playing. Measured file lengths: step_gravel x3 0.494 s (sound to -30 dB until 0.41-0.46 s), step_leaves x3 0.49-0.52 s, step_mud x3 0.494 s (mud_2/mud_3 are silent after 0.23/0.19 s: padded tails), step_snow_2 0.494, step_dirt 0.469 (silent after 0.19). Grass/wood/water takes are 0.10-0.30 s, so on gravel, leaves, mud and snow footsteps are heard at half the rate and in an uneven rhythm compared to grass.
fix: In Music.step, let a new step cut the old one (stop and restart, or alternate two step players) instead of skipping when _steps.playing; and trim step_* takes to <= 0.25 s with a 30 ms fade (add a step_ length cap to sfx_soften.py, e.g. trim trailing audio below -40 dB and hard-cap at 0.28 s with fade-out) so they never overlap at run pace.

title: Near-identical or broken takes: crit/crit_2 are the same impact (xcorr 0.88, spectra within 1.7 dB), swing x3 near-identical (xcorr 0.60-0.75), pop_3 is a truncated 15 ms click ending at 70% amplitude
repro: Cross-correlated every take pair of each name (normalised peak xcorr + 39-band log spectrum RMS diff). No md5 duplicates, but crit.ogg vs crit_2.ogg xcorr 0.877 / spectral diff 1.67 dB (source Impact_01 and Impact_02 from 150-combat-sound-effects are the same hit), so 2 of 3 crit plays sound identical. swing (swish-1..3) pairs 0.60-0.75, all three 70-120 ms, centroid ~230 Hz: the most frequent tool/attack sound has effectively one take. pop_3.ogg (bubbles-pop/pop.ogg) is 0.015 s long, last 20 samples at 0.7 of peak: an audible click with no body; pop_2 is 0.038 s. pop is used by 13 call sites (arcade, turrets, helpers, fallback).
fix: In tools/cc0_import.py MAP: crit -> replace Impact_02 with a distinct heavy hit (e.g. 37-hitspunches or 5-break-crunch-impacts); swing -> take swishes from air-whoosh / 20-sword-sound-effects-attacks-and-clashes (whoosh only) or 3-melee-sounds for 2 of 3 takes; pop -> replace bubbles-pop/pop.ogg with a ~80-120 ms pop (e.g. 3-pop-sounds pop3 or 40-cc0-water-splash-slime-sfx blip). Re-import with --only crit,swing,pop, then sfx_soften.py --only ... --force.

title: Worst 30 sounds by loud high end (>4 kHz level as played): the cash family, pin_crash_3, tools_3/tools_2 (default crafting-station sound), reel, rock_break, timber still bite after softening
repro: Ranked every non-jingle .ogg by in-game 10 ms peak loudness (file level -4 dB bus + GROUP_DB) plus 10*log10(share of energy above 4 kHz / 8 kHz). Worst 30: cash_pickup hf>4k -16.9 dB, >8k -17.4 dB, cen 9086 Hz, pk -1.0; sword_clash_2(unused) hf>4k -14.9 dB, >8k -19.7 dB, cen 6495 Hz, pk -2.6; cash_pickup_3 hf>4k -17.2 dB, >8k -17.6 dB, cen 10022 Hz, pk -1.5; pin_crash_3 hf>4k -16.7 dB, >8k -18.6 dB, cen 10428 Hz, pk -0.7; cash_register hf>4k -17.3 dB, >8k -18.5 dB, cen 7698 Hz, pk -2.1; cash_pickup_2 hf>4k -17.8 dB, >8k -18.1 dB, cen 8577 Hz, pk 0.3; sword_clash_3(unused) hf>4k -16.4 dB, >8k -20.6 dB, cen 6936 Hz, pk -2.8; tools_3 hf>4k -16.3 dB, >8k -21.5 dB, cen 5864 Hz, pk -2.9; reel hf>4k -19.2 dB, >8k -21.0 dB, cen 8339 Hz, pk -5.5; terminal_2 hf>4k -19.2 dB, >8k -21.0 dB, cen 6805 Hz, pk -2.9; cash_register_2 hf>4k -20.1 dB, >8k -20.7 dB, cen 4848 Hz, pk -2.1; rock_break hf>4k -18.2 dB, >8k -23.1 dB, cen 2296 Hz, pk -1.2; cash hf>4k -19.9 dB, >8k -22.9 dB, cen 5450 Hz, pk -3.3; unsheathe_3(unused) hf>4k -18.2 dB, >8k -25.5 dB, cen 6773 Hz, pk -4.3; timber hf>4k -20.5 dB, >8k -24.2 dB, cen 2083 Hz, pk -2.6; cash_register_3 hf>4k -21.2 dB, >8k -23.6 dB, cen 6092 Hz, pk -1.1; cloth_2 hf>4k -21.8 dB, >8k -23.2 dB, cen 3693 Hz, pk -4.7; bug_3 hf>4k -18.4 dB, >8k -26.8 dB, cen 4389 Hz, pk -1.9; alarm_2 hf>4k -22.5 dB, >8k -23.0 dB, cen 4721 Hz, pk -5.8; tools_2 hf>4k -21.3 dB, >8k -24.3 dB, cen 4328 Hz, pk -3.7; door_2 hf>4k -21.2 dB, >8k -25.5 dB, cen 3353 Hz, pk -2.8; reel_2 hf>4k -21.8 dB, >8k -25.2 dB, cen 6574 Hz, pk -4.3; dig hf>4k -21.4 dB, >8k -26.2 dB, cen 3325 Hz, pk -2.6; unlock_2 hf>4k -19.3 dB, >8k -28.6 dB, cen 3065 Hz, pk -2.4; hammer_3 hf>4k -20.3 dB, >8k -27.9 dB, cen 3725 Hz, pk -2.1; plant_3 hf>4k -20.9 dB, >8k -28.1 dB, cen 4182 Hz, pk -4.0; pin_crash_2 hf>4k -22.2 dB, >8k -26.9 dB, cen 2529 Hz, pk -1.4; unsheathe_2(unused) hf>4k -20.4 dB, >8k -28.8 dB, cen 5276 Hz, pk -2.6; sword_clash(unused) hf>4k -15.9 dB, >8k -33.6 dB, cen 5875 Hz, pk -3.3; twig_2 hf>4k -22.2 dB, >8k -27.3 dB, cen 6695 Hz, pk -2.5. Notes: tools/tools_2/tools_3 is CraftScreen.station_sound's fallback, so any station not in its table (most workshop stations) plays it; reel plays on every fish caught (98% energy above 4 kHz even after the 8.5 kHz low-pass, because the source is a ratchet hiss); rock_break take 1 is ~10 dB hotter than takes 2/3 and plays on every rock/ore hit; sword_clash/unsheathe are unused (no call site).

(2) sfx_soften.py: when hf > 0.6 after filtering, apply a second pass: low-pass 6 kHz + -6 dB shelf at 3.5 kHz and lower the level target by 3 dB (bright sounds read louder than RMS says); add TARGETS ('cash', -19), ('reel', -21), ('tools', -19), ('rock_break', -18). Run with --only cash,cash_2,cash_3,tools,tools_2,tools_3,reel,reel_2,rock_break,timber,terminal_2,bug_3,cloth_2,alarm_2,door_2,dig,unlock_2,hammer_3,plant_3,twig_2 --force. (3) Replace reel/reel_2 with a softer click-whirr (CC0 '87-clickety-clips' or '68-workshop-sounds' ratchet at lower pitch) and tools_3 with a wood/hammer tap from '100-cc0-metal-and-wood-sfx' via cc0_import.py MAP. (4) Optional: drop the unused sword_clash*/unsheathe* from the export or wire them (they are the harshest files in the folder). NOTE: see c6_05_13: --force on already-softened files stacks the filters; apply the c6_05_13 sfx_soften changes first and reprocess from source.
audio_needed: CC0 replacements for reel, reel_2, tools_3 (from packs already listed in tools/cc0_sources.json)

title: Takes of one sound differ by 6-17 dB or swing from dull to bright, so the random take picker makes the same action jump in level: servo (16.7 dB), cash (10.6), rock_break (10.4), spell_ice (8.1), chest_open (7.3), drop (6.9), fireworks, freeze (6.7), bubble, pickup (5.8)
repro: Per name, compared each take's in-game 10 ms peak loudness and >4 kHz share. servo -31.7 vs servo_2 -15.0 (servo take 1 is 99.9% energy above 4 kHz: a thin whine nearly inaudible next to take 2); cash -18.0/-15.0/-25.6 (the shop purchase sound in both arcs); rock_break -11.7/-22.1/-20.5; chest_open -13.1 (dull thump) vs chest_open_2 -20.4 (bright creak, 0.61 hf); pickup -23.0/-19.0/-24.8 with hf 0.24/0.47/0.76; pin_crash hf 0.05/0.22/0.97; terminal hf 1.0/0.77/0.20; seagull 0.00/0.79/0.53. sfx_soften.py levels each file to the group target from its loudest 100 ms RMS only, so short transient takes and long tails land far apart.
fix: In sfx_soften.py add a take-matching pass: for each base name with _2/_3, after per-file processing, match the takes to their median on the 10 ms peak loudness (within +-2 dB) and pull the brightest take's high shelf down until its hf is within 0.25 of the median. Run it with --force on the listed names. Where one take is a different sound (servo, chest_open_2, seagull, pin_crash_3, terminal), replace that take instead (cc0_import.py MAP / make_rec_audio.py).

title: GROUP_DB double-attenuates sounds sfx_soften already lowered: keypress plays at ~-37 dB and stink/servo at -29..-33, 13+ dB under the music bed, effectively inaudible on a phone speaker
repro: sfx_soften TARGETS already set ui_/menu_/talk_blip/keypress/step_ to -20 and page/equip to -19 (vs -16 default). Music.GROUP_DB then subtracts another 3.5-10 dB on top of the -4 dB voice: keypress (hack_game.gd every key) lands at -36.9 dB loudest-100ms, equip -30..-33, ui_tap -27, talk_blip -28. Music plays at MUSIC_DB -8 on -16 LUFS files (~-24). stink/stink_2 (status effect, game_map.gd:2147) were boosted the +6 dB max but the 8.5 kHz low-pass removed their content: -29 dB in game; servo (claw machine) -33. Footsteps: STEP_DB -14 + STEP_GROUND_DB -4 on files at -20 = about -38 for grass, -35 for stone.
fix: Pick one place for per-group level: either drop GROUP_DB values to the difference you still want (e.g. keypress -10 -> -3, ui_ -5 -> -2, equip -5 -> -2, talk_blip -5.5 -> -2.5) or set the soften TARGETS for those groups back to -16 and keep GROUP_DB. Replace stink/stink_2 and servo with sounds that have midrange body (CC0 '40-cc0-water-splash-slime-sfx' squelch for stink, '68-workshop-sounds' motor for servo) instead of boosting filtered hiss. Check footsteps against the music by ear; consider STEP_DB -10.

title: Jingles (j_*) are skipped by sfx_soften and have GROUP_DB 0, so they peak at -0.5..-1.5 dBFS and play 4-9 dB louder than every other effect and ~10 dB over the music, with no music duck under them
repro: Measured in-game loudest-100ms: j_region -11.1 (first visit to any new area), j_page -11.4 (journal page / lost bowling game), j_campaign_won -12.2, j_treasure -13.0, j_battle_start -14.8 (10 ms -10.8), j_confirm 10 ms -11.2 (whack GO), vs normal effects -17..-22 and music around -24 (MUSIC_DB -8 on -16 LUFS). The 2-3 s melodic jingles sit on top of the area song in an unrelated key; Music.set_duck exists but no jingle uses it. Short single effects levelup.ogg/quest_done.ogg/craft_done.ogg are ~-18.5, so the 'big moment' sounds are inconsistent too.
fix: In scripts/music.gd set GROUP_DB 'j_': -4.0 (or a -14 dB loudest-100ms target for j_* in ace_kits.py's import), and in Music.sfx when the name begins with 'j_' and the stream is longer than 1 s, dip the music ~6 dB for the stream length (tween _player.volume_db to MUSIC_DB + _duck - 6, back after get_length()), as Stardew does for its fanfares.

title: Some takes start with 140-150 ms of silence, so one in three hits/reloads lands late: crit_3 (147 ms), block_3 (143 ms), reload_2 (149 ms); die_3, step_mud_2, ball_return, whimper_2 carry 0.17-0.36 s silent tails
repro: Scanned every .ogg for the first/last sample above -50 dB of its peak. crit is used by farm.gd:1269 (critical crop/ hit), block by arcade_stack.gd:274 and block_jumper.gd:264 (per landed block: a late block thunk is very noticeable in a timing game), reload by player.gd:1355. Silent tails keep a voice busy (6-voice pool) for nothing.
fix: Add a trim step to sfx_soften.py (before the level pass): cut leading audio below -45 dB of peak (keep 3 ms pre-roll) and trailing audio below -50 dB, then the existing 3 ms fades; rerun with --only crit_3,block_3,reload_2,die_3,step_mud_2,ball_return,whimper_2 --force.

title: All 54 generated .wav placeholders in audio/sfx are shadowed by real .ogg files and never play (Music._load_sfx only falls back to .wav when no .ogg take exists), yet ship in the build; 11 .ogg sounds have no call site (cannon, crop_ready, door_close, growl, grunt, new_item, save_done, shop_bell, snore, sword_clash, unsheathe)
repro: Every audio/sfx/*.wav has a same-named .ogg (alert, bark, ... zap). grep -w of each base name across scripts/*.gd and data/*.json finds no use for the 11 listed (step_* are built dynamically and excluded). sword_clash*/unsheathe* are among the harshest files in the folder (0.77-0.99 of energy above 4 kHz).
fix: Add audio/sfx/*.wav (and the unused .ogg names) to the web export exclude filter, or have make_audio.py skip names that have a real .ogg; extend tools/sfx_audit.py to print unused sounds as a warning. Alternatively wire the useful ones: shop_bell on shop door open, door_close on leaving interiors, crop_ready on the morning ripe report, save_done on save, new_item on first-time pickups.

title: No limiter or compressor on any bus: SFX peaks sit at -1.5..-3 dBFS (13 files at -1..+0.3) and up to 6 SFX voices + step voice + music + ambience sum straight into Master, so busy fights and cash bursts can clip into phone-speaker distortion
repro: default_bus_layout.tres defines Music/SFX/Ambience with no effects; Master has none. Music.sfx plays every voice at -4 dB with no headroom management. Measured file peaks: median about -2.8 dBFS after softening, jingles -0.5..-1.5, cash_pickup_2 +0.3. Three overlapping hits/rock breaks (each 10 ms peak around -12..-11 dB in game, peaks -1.2..-2 dBFS before the -4 dB) plus a jingle exceed 0 dBFS.
fix: Add an AudioEffectHardLimiter (ceiling -1 dB, release ~0.1 s) to Master in default_bus_layout.tres, and a gentle AudioEffectCompressor on SFX (threshold -12 dB, ratio 3:1, attack 5 ms, release 120 ms) so stacked effects glue instead of spiking. No code change needed beyond the bus file.

title: When all 6 SFX voices are busy, Music.sfx swaps the stream on the oldest playing voice mid-sound: an abrupt cut (click) on the old sound, and talk blips always steal round-robin even when a voice is free
repro: music.gd ~353-362: pick = _sfx[_next_voice % size] while it is playing, then pick.stream = st with no fade; blip() (music.gd ~452) always takes _sfx[_next_voice % size] without checking for a free voice, so a dialogue line can cut off a jingle or a quest_done fanfare that is still ringing.
fix: In blip(), look for a free voice first like sfx() does (or give blips their own AudioStreamPlayer as steps have). For stealing, prefer the voice with the least time left (get_playback_position vs stream length) and never steal a j_* voice; optionally a 2-voice AudioStreamPolyphonic for blips.

title: sfx_soften.py measures loudness as plain RMS and boosts up to +6 dB after filtering, so bright sounds come back up: 51 files got the 8.5 kHz low-pass and many then +6 dB (reel, stink, stink_2, servo, cash_register, pin_crash_3 in a dry run); --force also re-filters already-softened files (effects stack)
repro: Dry-ran sfx_soften.process() on copies in /tmp/c6_05/try (worktree untouched). cash_pickup: hf 0.73 -> 0.15, rms -15.3 -> -18.4: works. But cash_register: hf 0.91 -> 0.65 with gain +6.0; pin_crash_3 hf 0.97 -> 0.78, gain +6.0; reel (already softened once, +6 then too) gets another 8.5 kHz pass and +6.0 again; tools_3 (already softened) +3.8. SOFTEN_LOG shows reel/stink/stink_2/servo all at gain_db 6.0. Plain RMS under-reads energy at 2-8 kHz (where the ear is most sensitive), so the louder-than-it-measures sounds are exactly the ones turned up. And because the filter runs on whatever is in the file, --force on a softened file low-passes it twice. From SOFTEN_LOG: 35 of the harshest files were low-passed (<= 8.5 kHz) AND boosted >= +3 dB: bug_3, cash, cash_3, chest_open_2, eat_2, eat_3, equip, equip_2, glass_3, harvest_2, harvest_3, keys, pickup_3, pin_tap_2, plant, plant_2, plant_3, reel, reel_2, servo, spell_ice_3, splash, step_leaves x3, step_mud, stink, stink_2, terminal_2, terminal_3, tools, tools_2, tools_3, twig_2, unsheathe_2.
fix: In sfx_soften.py: (1) measure loudness K-weighted (ffmpeg `ebur128=peak=true` momentary max, or apply a 1.5 kHz +4 dB high-shelf before the 100 ms RMS) instead of plain RMS; (2) cap upward gain at 0 dB when the post-filter hf > 0.5 (never boost a bright sound); (3) for hf > 0.6 use lowpass 6500 + shelf -8 dB at 3.5 kHz; (4) make --force start from the original source: keep the pre-soften file's md5 in the log and refuse --force on an already-softened file unless --from-source re-imports it first (cc0_import.py --only / make_rec_audio.py), so filters never stack. Then reprocess the 51 files with lowpass 8500 from source.

title: 38 effects have 75-100% of their energy below 350 Hz, which phone speakers barely reproduce: every swing take (96-99%), watering water_2 (96%), spell_fire x3, emp x3, zap_3, stomp, roar x3, step_wood, heartbeat - leveled 'to target' by RMS but near-silent or a dull thump on Tom's phone
repro: FFT energy share below 350 Hz per file (22.05 kHz decode). Over 75%: ball_return, book, bowl_gutter/pit/roll/rumble, car_door, cards, chest_open, cloth (98%), emp/emp_2/emp_3, grunt/grunt_2, heartbeat (100%), hit_3, horse, purr, roar x3, snore_2, spell_fire x3, spell_lightning_3, spell_nature_2, step_wood/_2, stomp (100%), swing/swing_2/swing_3 (96-99%, centroid ~230 Hz), teleport_2, thud_2, water_2, zap_3. swing is played on every tool/weapon swing; water_2 is a watering-can take. The soften pass high-passes only at 50 Hz and levels on RMS dominated by this bass, so the audible part sits 10-20 dB lower than the number says. Tom plays only on a phone.
fix: In sfx_soften.py add a phone-translation step: measure the level after a 300 Hz high-pass (what a phone speaker plays) and use that for the gain target; for files with >75% energy under 350 Hz add a +4..6 dB peak at 1.5-3 kHz (presence) and a 120 Hz high-pass, or layer a soft 2-4 kHz transient. Better for swing: replace the takes with real air swishes that have 1-6 kHz content (CC0 'air-whoosh', '20-sword-sound-effects-attacks-and-clashes' whoosh-only files) via tools/cc0_import.py MAP, then soften. Verify by listening through a 300 Hz high-pass (ffplay -af highpass=f=300).
audio_needed: CC0 replacements for swing x3 (and optionally spell_fire, emp) with midrange content

title: Music._load_sfx picks a take with randi() % n, so the same take repeats back-to-back a third of the time (half for 2-take sounds): with the near-identical takes above, rapid actions (chop, mine, swing, pickup) sound stamped
repro: music.gd _load_sfx: return t[randi() % t.size()]; no memory of the last take. Pitch drift (0.93-1.07) only applies to sounds under 0.45 s and not to coin/jingles.
fix: Keep a per-name last index (_last_take dict) and pick from the other takes (shuffle-bag), e.g. var i := randi() % (n - 1); if i >= last: i += 1. Same in RecAudio.lane_sound's take pick.

title: Same recording under two names: boss_down.ogg is the j_victory fanfare (xcorr 0.90), so a boss kill plays the 2.6 s victory jingle on death and again 2 s later as DangerMusic's STING; every mine guardian kill also plays a full victory fanfare. Also pin_tap_3 = thud_3, sleep = j_morning, craft_done = j_skill
repro: Cross-name fingerprint (30-band spectrum within 3 dB, then normalised xcorr): boss_down vs j_victory 0.903 (both 2.58 s), pin_tap_3 vs thud_3 0.920, j_morning vs sleep 0.904 (2.42 s), craft_done vs j_skill 0.865 (2.52 s). enemy.gd:736 plays boss_down for any `big` foe (bossy, is_guardian or boss_name) at death; danger_music.gd tick() then plays STING j_victory BOSS_WIND (2 s) later after boss_ended -> the same fanfare twice, overlapping its own tail. Mine guardians (MineKeepers lead) are is_guardian, so each floor's guardian gets a 2.6 s fanfare.
fix: Give boss_down a real impact/collapse sound (short, 0.6-0.9 s: a heavy thud + debris, e.g. CC0 '5-break-crunch-impacts' or '35-wooden-crackshitsdestructions'), keep j_victory only as the DangerMusic sting. In enemy.gd play boss_down only for bossy/boss_name and a lighter sound (crit or die) for plain guardians. In ace_kits.py stop writing the same render to two names (pick a different render or delete the duplicate: thud_3 or pin_tap_3, sleep vs j_morning).

title: The low-health warning heartbeat.ogg is 100% energy below 350 Hz (centroid 95 Hz): on a phone speaker the only audio cue that you are under 25% HP is inaudible; watering (farm.gd:1372) gets water_2 (centroid 319 Hz, 96% sub-350) one time in two
repro: player.gd:1420 plays heartbeat when a hit leaves HP under max/4. heartbeat.ogg: 1.1 s, centroid 95 Hz, all energy under 350 Hz. Phone speakers roll off below ~300-500 Hz, so Tom hears nothing. water.ogg (centroid 3.2 kHz) vs water_2.ogg (319 Hz) are two different sounds for the same can pour.
fix: Replace heartbeat with a heartbeat that has a click/knock transient in 1-3 kHz (or add a band-passed 1.5 kHz copy of each beat at -10 dB in sfx_soften via a per-name 'presence' list), and replace water_2 with a pour/sprinkle in the 1-6 kHz range (CC0 '40-cc0-water-splash-slime-sfx' or '6-short-water-splashes') via cc0_import.py MAP. Part of the phone-translation pass in c6_05_14.

title: 'sparkle' (47 call sites: rare fish, gems, block jumper, rewards) has no shimmer: all three takes carry ~0% energy above 4 kHz, peaking at 250 Hz-1 kHz (slices of an ACE bell kit), so the reward sparkle reads as a dull bell thud
repro: Band energy (dB rel. total) sparkle.ogg: <250 -36.6, 250-500 -5.8, 0.5-1k -1.9, 1-2k -10.5, 2-4k -32.7, 4-8k -35.1; sparkle_2 strongest below 250 Hz (-2.3); sparkle_3 2-4k -6.3 but 4-8k -27. Source: ace_kits.py kit_bells slices ('sparkle', 3, 0.1). sfx_soften did nothing wrong here (lowpass 14 kHz, hf before already 0.0).
fix: In ace_kits.py take the sparkle hits from a higher bell/glock render (or pitch the slices up an octave with asetrate+atempo and add a short 6-10 kHz shimmer tail at -18 dB), or import a CC0 chime (e.g. 'bell-dingschimes' or '50-rpg-sound-effects' magic chime) through cc0_import.py MAP; then sfx_soften --only sparkle. Aim for energy centred 2-5 kHz with a soft 6-9 kHz tail (bright but below the hf>0.6 harsh band).

title: Claw machine servo retriggers ~6-7 times a second while you steer, alternating at random between a near-silent 12 kHz whine (servo, -32 dB) and a loud motor (servo_2, -15 dB), and eats the SFX voices
repro: arcade_claw.gd:125-126: while a direction is held, sfx('servo') fires whenever int(phase_t*10) % 3 == 0, i.e. for 6 consecutive frames every 0.3 s; Music.sfx's 70 ms same-name guard lets 1-2 through per window, each 0.29-0.47 s long, so overlapping copies stack on the 6 voices. Takes measured: servo.ogg centroid 11.8 kHz, 99.9% energy above 4 kHz, -31.7 dB in game (10 ms); servo_2.ogg centroid 1.8 kHz, -15.0 dB: a 17 dB jump between consecutive triggers.
fix: Play the servo as one looping motor while steering: a dedicated AudioStreamPlayer in ArcadeClaw started when dir != 0 and stopped (60 ms fade) when released, pitch following speed; or at least trigger once per 0.3 s on an edge (track last slot). Replace servo.ogg (the whine) with a second motor take near servo_2's level and spectrum.
